what_this_is: One real track, measured, failed, fixed, measured again. Lyria 3 Pro generated the audio over the Gemini API on 2026-08-11. Every number here comes from services/audio/features.py via pyloudnorm — the same ITU-R BS.1770 code the deployed audio service runs. Nothing was typed by hand and nothing was rounded to look better.

source_track.credential_note: A C2PA manifest travels inside the returned MP3: a signed claim with a chain to a Google C2PA root and an RFC 3161 timestamp. GHARANA locates and digests it, and does NOT validate the signature — present, not checked. Re-encoding strips it, so the excerpts below carry none; that is a fact about the encoder, not the origin.

the_fix.why: The overshoot was small enough that a straight trim clears the -1.0 dBTP ceiling AND lands loudness inside the -14 +/- 1 LUFS window. Reaching for a limiter would have squashed dynamics nothing asked us to squash.
the_fix.what_it_did_not_fix: Loudness moved from -13.48 to -14.68 LUFS. Both pass, but the track is now quieter and closer to the bottom of tolerance. That is a trade the artist should see, not one to hide behind two green ticks.

measured_by.not_the_browser: The widget this replaced ran an AnalyserNode FFT and showed RMS. RMS is not LUFS and a browser cannot compute BS.1770 — the one place the product demonstrated its central claim was the one place it was not doing it.
